resolution: Implemented the static instance buffer (the fix for the 776k-instance per-frame re-upload choke). Added a retained INSTANCE path mirroring the existing g_retained_vbuf vertex cache: new Node flag scene3d_instance_static (framework/layout.zig); the no-V8 loader sets it on its box+ramp world batches (world_loader.zig, both built once at construct and never mutated). In framework/gpu/3d.zig drawScene Pass 2, a static batch routes to a new resolveStaticInstances() which stages + uploads it ONCE to a lazily-created g_static_inst_buf (MAX_STATIC_INSTANCES=1,048,576, ~80MB, keyed by data pointer, streamed in MAX_INSTANCES-sized chunks through g_inst_scratch), then every subsequent frame just binds + draws from it with ZERO restage/upload. Correct because makeInstance builds a model-only matrix (the camera lives in per-frame SceneUniforms), so a cached instance still tracks the moving camera. Also refined the req_0365 raise: reverted MAX_INSTANCES (the DYNAMIC per-frame buffer) from 1M back to 65536 — the static world no longer rides it, so every cart's dynamic buffer is lean 5.2MB again — and kept the staging scratch off the stack as the BSS global g_inst_scratch. Net memory: non-static carts ~10MB; the scale lab +80MB lazy static. First frame still pays one upload (~12 chunks at 776k); frames 2+ are free, which should take 512 blocks from choppy to flat-out. ast-check passes on all three Zig files; full type-check is the user's loader rebuild. Files: framework/gpu/3d.zig, framework/layout.zig, world_loader.zig. Pending the user's rebuild + playtest at --blocks 512.
